Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-119", "title": "Crohn's Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Crohn's disease is a chronic (long-lasting) disease that causes inflammation in your digestive tract."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It can affect any part of your digestive tract, which runs from your mouth to your anus."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "But it usually affects your small intestine and the beginning of your large intestine."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Crohn's disease is an inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Ulcerative colitis and microscopic colitis are other common types of IBD."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The cause of Crohn's disease is unknown."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Researchers think that an autoimmune reaction may be one cause."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "An autoimmune reaction happens when your immune system attacks healthy cells in your body."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Genetics may also play a role, since Crohn's disease can run in families."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Stress and eating certain foods don't cause the disease, but they can make your symptoms worse."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Who is more likely to develop Crohn's disease?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "There are certain factors that may raise your risk of Crohn's disease: Family history of the disease."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Having a parent, child, or sibling with the disease puts you at higher risk."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "This may double your risk of developing Crohn's disease."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Certain medicines , such as antibiotics , birth-control pills , and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as aspirin or ibuprofen."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "These may slightly increase your chance of developing Crohn's."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "This may also slightly increase your risk of Crohn's."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "What are the symptoms of Crohn's disease?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The symptoms of Crohn's disease can vary, depending where and how severe your inflammation is."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The most common symptoms include: Diarrhea Cramping and pain in your abdomen Weight loss Some other possible symptoms are: Anemia , a condition in which you have fewer red blood cells than normal Eye redness or pain Fatigue Fever Joint pain or soreness Nausea or loss of appetite Skin changes that involve red, tender bumps under the skin Stress and eating certain foods such as carbonated (fizzy) drinks and high-fiber foods may make some people's symptoms worse."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What other problems can Crohn's disease cause?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Crohn's disease can cause other problems, including: Intestinal obstruction , a blockage in the intestine Fistulas , abnormal connections between two parts inside of the body Abscesses , pus-filled pockets of infection Anal fissures, small tears in your anus that may cause itching, pain, or bleeding Ulcers, open sores in your mouth, intestines, anus, or perineum Malnutrition , when your body does not get the right amount of vitamins , minerals , and nutrients it needs Inflammation in other areas of your body, such as your joints, eyes, and skin How is Crohn's disease diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Your health care provider may use many tools to make a diagnosis: A medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms A family history A physical exam, including: Checking for bloating in your abdomen."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Listening to sounds within your abdomen using a stethoscope."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Tapping on your abdomen to check for tenderness and pain and to see if your liver or spleen is abnormal or enlarged."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Various tests, including: Blood and stool tests."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "An upper GI endoscopy, a procedure in which your provider uses a scope to look inside your mouth, esophagus, stomach, and small intestine."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Diagnostic imaging tests, such as a CT scan or an upper GI series."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "An upper GI series uses a special liquid called barium and x-rays ."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Drinking the barium will make your upper GI tract more visible on an x-ray."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "What are the treatments for Crohn's disease?"}, {"id": "S031", "text": "There is no cure for Crohn's disease, but treatments can decrease inflammation in your intestines, relieve symptoms, and prevent complications."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Treatments include medicines, bowel rest, and surgery."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "You and your provider can work together to figure out which treatment is best for you: Medicines for Crohn's include various medicines that decrease the inflammation."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Many of these medicines do this by reducing the activity of your immune system."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Certain medicines can also help with symptoms or complications, such as nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and anti-diarrheal medicines."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "If your Crohn's causes an infection, you may need antibiotics."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Bowel rest involves drinking only certain liquids or not eating or drinking anything."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "You may need to do this if your Crohn's disease symptoms are severe."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "You get your nutrients through drinking a liquid, a feeding tube, or an intravenous (IV) tube."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "You may need to do bowel rest in the hospital, or you may be able to do it at home."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "It will last for a few days or up to several weeks."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Surgery can treat complications and reduce symptoms when other treatments are not helping enough."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "The surgery will involve removing a damaged part of your digestive tract to treat: Fistulas Bleeding that is life threatening Intestinal obstructions Side effects from medicines when they threaten your health Symptoms when medicines do not improve your condition Changing your diet can help reduce symptoms."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Your provider may recommend that you make changes to your diet, such as: Avoiding carbonated drinks Avoiding popcorn, vegetable skins, nuts, and other high-fiber foods Drinking more liquids Eating smaller meals more often Keeping a food diary to help identify foods that cause problems In some cases, your provider may ask you to go on a special diet, such as a diet that is: High calorie Lactose free Low fat Low fiber Low salt If you are not absorbing enough nutrients, you may need to take nutritional supplements and vitamins."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-4274", "title": "Bone Grafts", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Surgeons use bone grafts to repair and rebuild diseased bones in your hips, knees, spine, and sometimes other bones and joints."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Grafts can also repair bone loss caused by some types of fractures (broken bones) or cancers."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Once your body accepts the bone graft, it provides a framework for growth of new, living bone."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "If the transplanted bone comes from another person , it is called an allograft."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Most allograft bone comes from donors who have died."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Tissue banks screen these donors and disinfect and test the donated bone to make sure it is safe to use."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "If the transplanted bone comes from another part of your own body, it is called an autograft."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Autograft bone often comes from your ribs, hips or a leg."}]}, {"id": "MLP-247", "title": "Eye Diseases", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Even if your eyes feel healthy, you could have a problem and not know it."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "That's why regular eye exams are so important."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Refractive errors are the most common type of vision problem that makes it hard to see clearly."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "But some eye conditions or diseases don't have any symptoms and can lead to a permanent loss of vision ."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some common eye diseases and conditions include: Cataracts , which happens when the clear lens in the front of your eye becomes cloudy."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Cataracts are common as you get older and can lead to vision loss."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Optic nerve disorders , which includes glaucoma ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Glaucoma usually happens when the fluid pressure inside your eyes slowly rises."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Retinal disorders , which are problems with the nerve layer at the back of your eye."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Macular degeneration , which is a disease that destroys your sharp, central vision."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Diabetic eye problems , which can cause vision loss and blindness."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Conjunctivitis , which is an infection also known as pink eye ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Some types of pink eye can spread very easily."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Some eye conditions and diseases do not always have symptoms."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Early detection through a comprehensive dilated eye exam could help your eye care provider detect diseases in the early stages."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Proper treatment could help slow or prevent vision loss."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Get regular eye exams and call your eye care professional right away if you notice any of these symptoms: A sudden change in vision Everything looks dim Flashes of light Eye pain Double vision Fluid coming from your eye Inflammation (swelling) Who is more likely to develop eye diseases?"}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Getting older increases your risk of some eye diseases."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Other things that may put you at a higher risk of some eye diseases can include if you: Are overweight or obese Have a family history of eye disease Are African American, Hispanic, or Native American Have certain health conditions such as Diabetic eye problems , or high blood pressure What are the treatments for eye diseases?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Treatment may depend on the eye condition or disease but can include: A new prescription for eyeglasses or contacts Use of bright lights or magnifying lenses for reading and other activities Medicines Prescription eye drops or ointments Laser treatment Surgery Depending on your eye condition or disease, treatment may slow vision loss but may not restore vision."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Talk to your provider about what treatment is best for you."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Your best defense is to have regular checkups."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Be sure to tell your provider if any eye diseases run in your family."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "You can also help take care of your vision by making lifestyle changes to lower your risk of health conditions that can cause vision problems."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "This could include by: Protecting your eyes from the sun Wearing protective eyewear while using tools or playing certain sports Getting regular physical activity Staying at a healthy weight Quitting smoking (or not starting) Eating a healthy diet NIH: National Eye Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5651", "title": "Meningococcal Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Meningococcal disease is the name for any illness that is caused by Neisseria meningitidis bacteria (also called meningococcal bacteria)."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "These illnesses are often severe and can sometimes be deadly."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They include infections of the lining of the brain and spinal cord ( meningitis ) and in the bloodstream ( sepsis )."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Some people have Neisseria meningitidis , the bacteria that cause the disease, in the back of their nose and throat."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "They usually have the bacteria but don't get sick."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "This is called being a \"carrier.\" But sometimes the bacteria can spread to other parts of the body and cause meningococcal disease."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The bacteria can spread from person to person through saliva (spit)."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "It usually happens through close or lengthy contact with a person who has it."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Close contact can include things like kissing and coughing."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "You cannot catch the bacteria through casual contact with someone who has the disease."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "For example, you cannot get it by breathing air where that person has been."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Who is more likely to get meningococcal disease?"}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Anyone can get meningococcal disease, but you are more likely to get it if someone you live with has it."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "You are also more likely to get it if you have direct contact with the saliva of someone who has it (like through kissing)."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Also, certain groups of people are more likely to get the disease."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "They include: Children younger than 1 year old."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Teens and young adults ages 16 through 23 years old."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "People with medical conditions that weaken their immune system , including those with HIV and certain rare immune system diseases."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "People who either don't have a spleen or have a spleen that does not function well."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "These are immunotherapy medicines that are given to people with certain rare conditions."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "People who live in crowded settings, such as college dorms or military barracks."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "People who travel to areas where the disease is more common, such as certain parts of sub-Saharan Africa."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "What are the symptoms of meningococcal disease?"}, {"id": "S023", "text": "There are different types of meningococcal disease."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "The most common types are meningitis and septicemia."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Both types are very serious and can be deadly in a matter of hours."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Meningococcal meningitis is a meningococcal infection of the lining of the brain and spinal cord."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "The most common symptoms include: Fever Headache Stiff neck It can also cause symptoms such as: Nausea and vomiting Photophobia (your eyes being more sensitive to light) Confusion It may be hard to notice these symptoms in newborns and babies."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "They may: Be slow or inactive Be irritable Vomit Feed poorly Have a bulging of the soft spot of their skull Meningococcal septicemia is a meningococcal infection of the bloodstream."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "When someone has this disease, the bacteria enter the bloodstream and multiply."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "This damages the walls of the blood vessels and causes bleeding into the skin and organs."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "The symptoms may include: Fever and chills Fatigue Vomiting Cold hands and feet Severe aches or pain in the muscles, joints, chest , or abdomen (belly) Rapid breathing Diarrhea A dark purple rash (in the later stages of the disease) Because it is so serious, you need to seek immediate medical attention if you or your child develops the symptoms of meningococcal disease."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "The signs and symptoms of meningococcal disease are often similar to those of other illnesses."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "If your (or your child's) health care provider thinks that you or your child could have meningococcal disease, they will order tests that take samples of blood and/or cerebrospinal fluid (fluid near the spinal cord)."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "They will send the samples to a lab for testing."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "The testing will include bacteria culture testing , which can identify the specific type of bacteria that is causing the infection."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Knowing this can help the provider decide on the best treatment."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "What are the treatments for meningococcal disease?"}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Certain antibiotics can treat meningococcal disease."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "It is important that treatment is started as soon as possible."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "So if the provider thinks you have meningococcal disease, they will give you antibiotics right away (before the test results come back)."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "People with serious disease may need additional treatments, such as: Breathing support Medicines to treat low blood pressure Surgery to remove dead tissue Wound care for parts of the body with damaged skin Some people with meningococcal disease will have long-term health problems and disabilities ."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "These may include: Loss of limb(s) Deafness Nervous system problems Brain damage Even with treatment, 10 to 15 in 100 people will die from the disease."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "The best way to prevent meningococcal disease is to get vaccinated."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends meningococcal vaccination for: All preteens and teens Children at higher risk for meningococcal disease Adults at higher risk for meningococcal disease If you are a close contact of a person with meningococcal disease, you will likely be given antibiotics to prevent you from getting sick."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "This is called \"prophylaxis.\" Close contacts include people who are living together."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "They also include people who had direct contact with the saliva of a person who has the disease (such as from kissing)."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "Although it's rare, you can get meningococcal disease more than once."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-3623", "title": "Emphysema", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Emphysema is a type of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease)."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "COPD is a group of lung diseases that make it hard to breathe and get worse over time."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The other main type of COPD is chronic bronchitis ."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Most people with COPD have both emphysema and chronic bronchitis, but how severe each type is can be different from person to person."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Emphysema affects the air sacs in your lungs."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Normally, these sacs are elastic or stretchy."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "When you breathe in, each air sac fills up with air, like a small balloon."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "When you breathe out, the air sacs deflate, and the air goes out."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "In emphysema, the walls between many of the air sacs in the lungs are damaged."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "This causes the air sacs to lose their shape and become floppy."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The damage also can destroy the walls of the air sacs, leading to fewer and larger air sacs instead of many tiny ones."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "This makes it harder for your lungs to move oxygen in and carbon dioxide out of your body."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The cause of emphysema is usually long-term exposure to irritants that damage your lungs and the airways."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "In the United States, cigarette smoke is the main cause."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Pipe, cigar, and other types of tobacco smoke can also cause emphysema, especially if you inhale them."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Exposure to other inhaled irritants can contribute to emphysema."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "These include secondhand smoke , air pollution , and chemical fumes or dusts from the environment or workplace."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Rarely, a genetic condition called alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency can play a role in causing emphysema."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The risk factors for emphysema include: Smoking."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Up to 75% of people who have emphysema smoke or used to smoke."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Long-term exposure to other lung irritants , such as secondhand smoke, air pollution, and chemical fumes and dusts from the environment or workplace."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Most people who have emphysema are at least 40 years old when their symptoms begin."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "This includes alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, which is a genetic condition."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Also, smokers who get emphysema are more likely to get it if they have a family history of COPD."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "At first, you may have no symptoms or only mild symptoms."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "As the disease gets worse, your symptoms usually become more severe."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "They can include: Frequent coughing or wheezing A cough that produces a lot mucus Shortness of breath, especially with physical activity A whistling or squeaky sound when you breathe Tightness in your chest Some people with emphysema get frequent respiratory infections such as colds and the flu ."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "In severe cases, emphysema can cause weight loss, weakness in your lower muscles, and swelling in your ankles, feet, or legs."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Your health care provider may use many tools to make a diagnosis: A medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms A family history Other tests, such as lung function tests , a chest x-ray or CT scan , and blood tests What are the treatments for emphysema?"}, {"id": "S029", "text": "However, treatments can help with symptoms, slow the progress of the disease, and improve your ability to stay active."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "There are also treatments to prevent or treat complications of the disease."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Treatments include: Lifestyle changes , such as Quitting smoking if you are a smoker."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "This is the most important step you can take to treat emphysema."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Avoiding secondhand smoke and places where you might breathe in other lung irritants Ask your health care provider for an eating plan that will meet your nutritional needs."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Also ask about how much physical activity you can do."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Physical activity can strengthen the muscles that help you breathe and improve your overall wellness."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Medicines , such as Bronchodilators, which relax the muscles around your airways."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "This helps open your airways and makes breathing easier."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Most bronchodilators are taken through an inhaler."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "In more severe cases, the inhaler may also contain steroids to reduce inflammation."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Vaccines for the flu and pneumococcal pneumonia, since people with emphysema are at higher risk for serious problems from these diseases Antibiotics if you get a bacterial or viral lung infection Oxygen therapy , if you have severe emphysema and low levels of oxygen in your blood."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Oxygen therapy can help you breathe better."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "You may need extra oxygen all the time or only at certain times."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Pulmonary rehabilitation , which is a program that helps improve the well-being of people who have chronic breathing problems."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "It may include An exercise program Disease management training Nutritional counseling Psychological counseling Surgery , usually as a last resort for people who have severe symptoms that have not gotten better with medicines."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "There are surgeries to Remove damaged lung tissue Remove large air spaces (bullae) that can form when air sacs are destroyed."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "The bullae can interfere with breathing."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "This is might be an option if you have very severe emphysema."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "If you have emphysema, it's important to know when and where to get help for your symptoms."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "You should get emergency care if you have severe symptoms, such as trouble catching your breath or talking."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Call your health care provider if your symptoms are getting worse or if you have signs of an infection, such as a fever ."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "Since smoking causes most cases of emphysema, the best way to prevent it is to not smoke."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "It's also important to try to avoid lung irritants such as secondhand smoke, air pollution, chemical fumes, and dusts."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}]
